subject: zone-tailed hawk
title: Lizards Ignore These Birds Overhead. One of Them Is a Hawk

scenes.text: Lizards and doves ignore these birds overhead. That's a mistake.
Turkey vultures only eat the dead, so small animals below have learned to ignore them.
But one bird in the flock is different. Same dark body, same V-shaped wings, same wobble.
It's a zone-tailed hawk, with four-foot wings, and it hunts live prey.
It drifts lower with the vultures, then drops in a sudden, steep attack.
So look again at the flock. Which one is the hawk?

description:
Zone-tailed hawks soar among turkey vultures and look almost exactly like them: dark body, wings held in a shallow V, the same rocking glide.
Small animals ignore vultures, which eat only carrion, so the hawk can drift close and then drop on live lizards, birds and small mammals. Biologists call it aggressive mimicry.
Would you spot the hawk in the flock?

first_comment: Zone-tailed hawks even nest near turkey vultures. What other predator hides in plain sight?
